name: Harper Road Technology Park
decision_label: Board removed data centers from the zoning code
summary: Peculiar reversed its zoning approach and removed data centers as a permitted use after organized local opposition, blocking Diode Ventures' planned Harper Road campus.
proposal_description: Diode Ventures discussed a hyperscale technology park near Harper Road. The city's review moved from enabling language to a moratorium and then removal of data centers from the zoning code.
site_afterlife: No verified replacement use for the proposed site is included. Citywide zoning treatment should be tracked separately from parcel-level economic outcomes.
evidence_note: The policy action is verified in the city's agenda packet. The causal link to one developer's final investment decision requires continued company and parcel research.
unresolved_questions: Does Diode Ventures or an affiliate still control the Harper Road acreage?
Were any transmission, water, or tax-incentive applications filed outside the city land-use process?
What use, if any, has replaced the technology-park concept on the 508-acre site?
Can Peculiar-level revenue and employment be separated from Cass County aggregates?

timeline.title: Technology-park concept enters public discussion
timeline.summary: Diode presented data-center development material during local planning review.

timeline.title: Planning Commission recommends underlying rezoning
timeline.summary: The commission recommended agricultural-to-light-industrial zoning while retaining overlay requirements; the action did not approve a final development plan or agreement.

timeline.title: Board advances zoning but not a final project
timeline.summary: Board materials describe Brad Hardin, Diode Ventures, roughly 508 acres, and the need for later project-specific approvals.

timeline.title: Board adopts a data-center application moratorium
timeline.summary: The city paused applications while reviewing health, safety, welfare, and zoning implications.

timeline.title: Public opposition fills local hearings
timeline.summary: Residents organized and turned out in large numbers as officials reconsidered whether data centers should remain an allowed use.

timeline.title: Board removes data centers from the zoning code
timeline.summary: The ordinance eliminated the use category that would have enabled the project.

timeline.title: City reports continued growth; exact counterfactual remains unknown
timeline.summary: A two-year retrospective found the data-center acreage still agricultural, documented new housing and businesses elsewhere in Peculiar, and confirmed the proposal never reached a final development plan or incentive agreement. Those observations do not isolate the decision's net economic effect.

county_outcome_context.note: The county panel ends in the October 2024 decision year, leaving zero full post-decision years. Cass County is larger than Peculiar and includes unrelated development, so future county trends will not be a clean measure of the city's zoning reversal.
